person.occupation: member of the Friends of Liberty

note.p: Bailey was a member of the Friends of Liberty, seceders from the London Corresponding Society in 1795. Bailey was seen with members of the LCS, including Thewall and Powell. The Friends of Liberty met at Shacklewell on the 20 July 1795. William Toone was the chairman, Joseph Burks the secretary, and Bailey delivered his lectured The White Devils Uncased, and Prince Brothers’ Scarlet Devils Displayed (referring to nobles), at sections 2 and 7 of the Friends of Liberty. They were printed and sold at radical bookstores including T Spence, F Place, and D I Eaton. A handwritten note on top of the copy of Scarlet Devils (in the Eighteenth Century Collections Online) states that F Ward of 41 Dean Street was prosecuted for selling it, the poetry was considered the most obnoxious part. The Bailey that Godwin saw was likely to be Citizen Bailey, and other entries also could be the same person. Citizen Bailey could be J C Bailey, who signed the Declaration of Friends to Liberty of the Press 1792, as did many LCS members. There was also an LCS member named Peter Bailey.
